name: profile
description: Profile a CSV file: frequency, series, exogenous columns and the recommended forecaster and estimator. Returns a profile id.

data_path.description: Absolute path of a CSV file inside the directory the server may read. URLs are not accepted.
data_path.title: Data Path

target.description: Column to forecast, or a list of columns (one series each) for wide multi-series data.
target.title: Target

date_column.description: Column with the dates. When null, the first column holding dates is used.
date_column.title: Date Column

series_id_column.description: Column with the series ids of long multi-series data.
series_id_column.title: Series Id Column

exog_columns.description: Columns to use as exogenous variables, an empty list for none. When null, every column that is not the target, the date or the series ids. The other columns are not used.
exog_columns.title: Exog Columns

ToolNotice.description:
A warning emitted while a tool call ran.

Attributes
----------
source : str
    Where the warning comes from: `'data'` (reading or profiling the
    data), `'plan'` (a warning the plan carries in `plan.warnings`, or
    the model a plan uses) or `'runtime'` (any other warning of the
    call).
category : str
    Class name of the warning (e.g. `'LongTrainingWarning'`), or
    `'ModelDownloadNotice'` for the notice of the server that a
    foundation model will download its weights.
message : str
    Text of the warning, without the suggestion of skforecast on how to
    silence it, cut to 1,000 characters.
count : int
    Number of times the call emitted it.
ToolNotice.title: ToolNotice

output_schema.description:
Envelope returned by the tools that create an object, and by
`describe_object`.

Attributes
----------
id : str
    Id of the object, to pass to the tools that take it.
kind : str
    Kind of the object: `'profile'`, `'plan'`, `'cv'`, `'backtest'`,
    `'comparison'` or `'forecast'`.
links : dict
    Ids of related objects: those it was built from (`profile_id`,
    `plan_id`, `cv_id`, and `parent_plan_id` for a refined plan), the
    plan of the winner of a comparison (`best_plan_id`), and the
    comparison a winning plan comes from (`comparison_id`).
summary : str
    Plain-text description of the object (`describe()` of the core),
    cut to 20,000 characters.
summary_truncated : bool
    Whether `summary` was cut; the full text is then in
    `files['summary']`.
notices : list of ToolNotice
    Warnings the call emitted, the first 20 distinct ones. Deprecation
    warnings go to the log of the server instead, and the failures of
    the candidates of a comparison are in its result.
notices_omitted : int
    Number of distinct warnings left out of `notices`.
files : dict
    Absolute paths of the files written for the object, by role:
    `predictions` and `metrics` (CSV with the index) of a backtest or a
    forecast, `leaderboard`, `best_predictions` and `best_metrics` of a
    comparison, and `summary` when the summary was cut.
values_included : bool
    Always False: the response holds no rows of the data or of the
    predictions. The summary carries statistics of the predictions, the
    metrics and the leaderboard of a comparison; the rows are in
    `files`.
cost : dict, None
    Cost of a cross-validation strategy, a backtest or a comparison:
    `n_folds`, `n_fits` (trainings of the forecaster in the shared
    strategy) and `estimator_fits` (fits of an estimator, which a
    direct forecaster multiplies by `steps`; for a comparison, the sum
    over its candidates). A cross-validation strategy also has
    `compare_estimator_fits`, the fits of a comparison without
    candidates with it. None for the other kinds.
changeable : list of str
    Arguments of `refine_plan` (for a plan) or of `create_cv` (for a
    cross-validation strategy) that build a variant of the object.
    Empty for the other kinds.
output_schema.title: ToolResult

name: plan
description: Build a forecasting plan (lags, window features, metric, preprocessing, interval) from a profile and a horizon. Returns a plan id.

steps.description: Forecast horizon: number of steps ahead to predict, from 1 to the length of the longest series (12 for a year of monthly data).
steps.title: Steps

interval.description: Prediction interval as two quantiles [lower, upper] with 0 < lower < upper < 1, e.g. [0.1, 0.9] for 80 %. The baseline and ForecasterStats only take symmetric ones (lower + upper = 1). Null for no interval.
interval.title: Interval

forecaster.description: skforecast forecaster class: ForecasterRecursive or ForecasterDirect (one series, machine learning), ForecasterRecursiveMultiSeries (several series), ForecasterDirectMultiVariate (one series predicted from several), ForecasterStats (Auto-ARIMA), ForecasterFoundation (pre-trained foundation model, no training) or ForecasterEquivalentDate (seasonal naive baseline). Null for the recommendation of the profile.
forecaster.title: Forecaster

estimator.description: Estimator: one of ['CatBoostRegressor', 'HistGradientBoostingRegressor', 'LGBMRegressor', 'RandomForestRegressor', 'Ridge', 'XGBRegressor'] for the machine learning forecasters, 'Arima' for ForecasterStats, or the Hugging Face model id of a foundation model for ForecasterFoundation (default 'autogluon/chronos-2-small'; model id prefixes: ['amazon/chronos-2', 'autogluon/chronos-2', 'google/timesfm-2.5', 'google/timesfm-3.0', 'Salesforce/moirai-2', 'soda-inria/tabicl', 'priorlabs/tabpfn', 'theforecastingcompany/t0', 'Synthefy/Nori', 'taharnbl/TS-ICL']). ForecasterEquivalentDate takes none. Null for the recommendation.
estimator.title: Estimator

estimator_kwargs.description: Keyword arguments of the estimator, e.g. {'n_estimators': 200}. A foundation model only takes context_length, cross_learning, point_estimate, max_horizon, add_calendar_features and n_fourier_terms. Null for the defaults.
estimator_kwargs.title: Estimator Kwargs

lags.description: Lags: an integer n for 1..n, or a list of distinct positive integers. Null for the selection from the partial autocorrelation.
lags.title: Lags

window_features.description: Rolling features, one entry per window size: {'stats': [...], 'window_size': n}, with stats among ['mean', 'std', 'min', 'max', 'sum', 'median', 'ratio_min_max', 'coef_variation', 'ewm'], e.g. [{'stats': ['mean', 'std'], 'window_size': 7}]. Null for the deterministic selection.
window_features.title: Window Features

metric.description: Metric, or list of metrics whose first one is the primary metric (the one that ranks); only the ones given are computed. Null for the metric selected from the data (MAE for one series, MASE for several) and its default panel.
metric.title: Metric

use_exog.description: Whether to use the exogenous columns of the data: false leaves them out (forecast then takes no exog_path); true fails when the data has none or the forecaster cannot use them. Null uses them whenever the forecaster can.
use_exog.title: Use Exog

differentiation.description: Order of differencing of the target before training (an integer of at least 1, usually 1 for a trend); predictions are integrated back. Machine learning forecasters only. Null for none.
differentiation.title: Differentiation

calendar_features.description: Calendar features generated from the dates (an empty list for none); the encoding follows the estimator. A feature whose column is already an exogenous column used by the plan is rejected. Machine learning forecasters with a datetime index only. Null for those selected from the frequency.
calendar_features.title: Calendar Features

target_transformer.description: Scaler of the target: 'StandardScaler', or 'none' for no scaling. Machine learning forecasters only. Null for the rule.
target_transformer.title: Target Transformer

dropna_from_series.description: Whether to drop the training rows with missing values; false fails when the data has missing values and the estimator does not accept them. Machine learning forecasters only. Null for the rule.
dropna_from_series.title: Dropna From Series

name: refine_plan
description: Build a new plan from an existing one, changing some of its decisions. Returns a new plan id; the original plan is kept.

RefinePlanArgs.description: Decisions of the plan to change. An omitted key keeps the value of the plan; every key but forecaster, estimator and steps set to null asks for the deterministic default.

forecaster.description: skforecast forecaster class: ForecasterRecursive or ForecasterDirect (one series, machine learning), ForecasterRecursiveMultiSeries (several series), ForecasterDirectMultiVariate (one series predicted from several), ForecasterStats (Auto-ARIMA), ForecasterFoundation (pre-trained foundation model, no training) or ForecasterEquivalentDate (seasonal naive baseline).
forecaster.title: Forecaster

estimator.description: Estimator: one of ['CatBoostRegressor', 'HistGradientBoostingRegressor', 'LGBMRegressor', 'RandomForestRegressor', 'Ridge', 'XGBRegressor'] for the machine learning forecasters, 'Arima' for ForecasterStats, or the Hugging Face model id of a foundation model for ForecasterFoundation (default 'autogluon/chronos-2-small'; model id prefixes: ['amazon/chronos-2', 'autogluon/chronos-2', 'google/timesfm-2.5', 'google/timesfm-3.0', 'Salesforce/moirai-2', 'soda-inria/tabicl', 'priorlabs/tabpfn', 'theforecastingcompany/t0', 'Synthefy/Nori', 'taharnbl/TS-ICL']). ForecasterEquivalentDate takes none.
estimator.title: Estimator

estimator_kwargs.description: Keyword arguments of the estimator, e.g. {'n_estimators': 200}. A foundation model only takes context_length, cross_learning, point_estimate, max_horizon, add_calendar_features and n_fourier_terms. Null for the defaults of the estimator.
estimator_kwargs.title: Estimator Kwargs

steps.description: Forecast horizon: number of steps ahead to predict, from 1 to the length of the longest series (12 for a year of monthly data).
steps.title: Steps

interval.description: Prediction interval as two quantiles [lower, upper] with 0 < lower < upper < 1, e.g. [0.1, 0.9] for 80 %. The baseline and ForecasterStats only take symmetric ones (lower + upper = 1). Null removes the interval.
interval.title: Interval

lags.description: Lags: an integer n for 1..n, or a list of distinct positive integers. Null selects them again from the partial autocorrelation.
lags.title: Lags

window_features.description: Rolling features, one entry per window size: {'stats': [...], 'window_size': n}, with stats among ['mean', 'std', 'min', 'max', 'sum', 'median', 'ratio_min_max', 'coef_variation', 'ewm'], e.g. [{'stats': ['mean', 'std'], 'window_size': 7}]. Null selects them again with the deterministic rules.
window_features.title: Window Features

metric.description: Metric, or list of metrics whose first one is the primary metric (the one that ranks); only the ones given are computed. Null selects them again from the data. Omitted, a metric chosen before is kept.
metric.title: Metric

use_exog.description: Whether to use the exogenous columns of the data: false leaves them out (forecast then takes no exog_path); true fails when the data has none or the forecaster cannot use them. Null lets the rule decide again. Omitted, a choice made before is kept.
use_exog.title: Use Exog

differentiation.description: Order of differencing of the target before training (an integer of at least 1, usually 1 for a trend); predictions are integrated back. Machine learning forecasters only. Null removes it. Omitted, an order chosen before is kept.
differentiation.title: Differentiation

calendar_features.description: Calendar features generated from the dates (an empty list for none); the encoding follows the estimator. A feature whose column is already an exogenous column used by the plan is rejected. Machine learning forecasters with a datetime index only. Null selects them again from the frequency. Omitted, a choice made before is kept.
calendar_features.title: Calendar Features

target_transformer.description: Scaler of the target: 'StandardScaler', or 'none' for no scaling. Machine learning forecasters only. Null lets the rule decide again. Omitted, a choice made before is kept.
target_transformer.title: Target Transformer

dropna_from_series.description: Whether to drop the training rows with missing values; false fails when the data has missing values and the estimator does not accept them. Machine learning forecasters only. Null lets the rule decide again. Omitted, a choice made before is kept.
dropna_from_series.title: Dropna From Series

RefinePlanArgs.title: RefinePlanArgs

plan_id.description: Id of the plan to refine.
plan_id.title: Plan Id

overrides.description: Values to change, e.g. {'estimator': 'Ridge', 'lags': 12}. An omitted key keeps the value of the plan; {'lags': null} selects the lags again and {'interval': null} removes the interval.

name: create_cv
description: Build a time series cross-validation strategy (TimeSeriesFold) for a plan. The response states its cost in `cost`. Returns a cv id.

plan_id.description: Id of the plan to backtest (from `plan` or `refine_plan`).
plan_id.title: Plan Id

initial_train_size.description: Observations of the first training set (a number), or the ISO 8601 date that ends it ('2005-06-01'). Null for the default: 70 % of the series, at least what the lags need and leaving room for two folds, written as a date when the data has dates.
initial_train_size.title: Initial Train Size

fold_stride.description: Observations the test set advances between folds. Null for `steps` (back-to-back folds); a larger value means fewer folds.
fold_stride.title: Fold Stride

refit.description: Whether to train again in every fold (true), never (false) or every n folds (an integer). Null for false: train once. Refitting multiplies the cost; ForecasterStats is refitted in every fold whatever it says.
refit.title: Refit

fixed_train_size.description: Whether the training window keeps its size when refitting (true) or grows (false). Null for false. Only with `refit` true or an integer: with `refit` false or null it is an error, as it would not run (ForecasterStats aside).
fixed_train_size.title: Fixed Train Size

gap.description: Observations between the end of training and the test set. Null for 0. A direct forecaster (ForecasterDirect, ForecasterDirectMultiVariate) cannot be backtested with a gap.
gap.title: Gap

skip_folds.description: Folds are numbered from 0, and fold 0 always runs. An integer n keeps folds 0, n, 2n, ...; a list skips the folds at those numbers (each at least 1 and below the number of folds). Null for every fold.
skip_folds.title: Skip Folds

allow_incomplete_fold.description: Whether the last fold may have fewer than `steps` observations. Null for true.
allow_incomplete_fold.title: Allow Incomplete Fold

name: compare
description: Backtest several configurations on the same folds and rank them by the metric of the profile. Reports progress per candidate and can be cancelled between candidates. Returns a comparison id and the plan of the winner in `links.best_plan_id`.

CandidateArg.description: A configuration to compare, with a unique name.

name.description: Unique name of the candidate, which labels its row of the leaderboard. 'Baseline (seasonal naive)' and 'Baseline (naive)' are reserved for the baseline.
name.title: Name

config.description: Its configuration; empty for the recommendation.

CandidateArg.title: CandidateArg

CandidateArgs.description: Configuration of one candidate. An omitted key keeps the recommendation of the profile.

forecaster.description: skforecast forecaster class: ForecasterRecursive or ForecasterDirect (one series, machine learning), ForecasterRecursiveMultiSeries (several series), ForecasterDirectMultiVariate (one series predicted from several), ForecasterStats (Auto-ARIMA), ForecasterFoundation (pre-trained foundation model, no training) or ForecasterEquivalentDate (seasonal naive baseline).
forecaster.title: Forecaster

estimator.description: Estimator: one of ['CatBoostRegressor', 'HistGradientBoostingRegressor', 'LGBMRegressor', 'RandomForestRegressor', 'Ridge', 'XGBRegressor'] for the machine learning forecasters, 'Arima' for ForecasterStats, or the Hugging Face model id of a foundation model for ForecasterFoundation (default 'autogluon/chronos-2-small'; model id prefixes: ['amazon/chronos-2', 'autogluon/chronos-2', 'google/timesfm-2.5', 'google/timesfm-3.0', 'Salesforce/moirai-2', 'soda-inria/tabicl', 'priorlabs/tabpfn', 'theforecastingcompany/t0', 'Synthefy/Nori', 'taharnbl/TS-ICL']). ForecasterEquivalentDate takes none.
estimator.title: Estimator

estimator_kwargs.description: Keyword arguments of the estimator, e.g. {'n_estimators': 200}. A foundation model only takes context_length, cross_learning, point_estimate, max_horizon, add_calendar_features and n_fourier_terms.
estimator_kwargs.title: Estimator Kwargs

lags.description: Lags: an integer n for 1..n, or a list of distinct positive integers. Null selects them from the partial autocorrelation.
lags.title: Lags

window_features.description: Rolling features, one entry per window size: {'stats': [...], 'window_size': n}, with stats among ['mean', 'std', 'min', 'max', 'sum', 'median', 'ratio_min_max', 'coef_variation', 'ewm'], e.g. [{'stats': ['mean', 'std'], 'window_size': 7}]. Null selects them with the deterministic rules.
window_features.title: Window Features

use_exog.description: Whether to use the exogenous columns of the data: false leaves them out (forecast then takes no exog_path); true fails when the data has none or the forecaster cannot use them. Null uses them whenever the forecaster can.
use_exog.title: Use Exog

differentiation.description: Order of differencing of the target before training (an integer of at least 1, usually 1 for a trend); predictions are integrated back. Machine learning forecasters only. The candidate runs on a copy of the strategy with this order.
differentiation.title: Differentiation

calendar_features.description: Calendar features generated from the dates (an empty list for none); the encoding follows the estimator. A feature whose column is already an exogenous column used by the plan is rejected. Machine learning forecasters with a datetime index only. Null selects them from the frequency.
calendar_features.title: Calendar Features

target_transformer.description: Scaler of the target: 'StandardScaler', or 'none' for no scaling. Machine learning forecasters only. Null for the rule.
target_transformer.title: Target Transformer

dropna_from_series.description: Whether to drop the training rows with missing values; false fails when the data has missing values and the estimator does not accept them. Machine learning forecasters only. Null for the rule.
dropna_from_series.title: Dropna From Series

CandidateArgs.title: CandidateArgs

cv_id.description: Id returned by `create_cv`: every candidate is backtested on its folds.
cv_id.title: Cv Id

candidates.description: Configurations to compare, each {'name': ..., 'config': {...}}, e.g. [{'name': 'ridge', 'config': {'estimator': 'Ridge'}}]. Null for the candidates recommended by the profile: the forecasters of its family (with several series, ForecasterRecursiveMultiSeries and ForecasterFoundation), or the estimators of the recommended forecaster when that leaves one, without those above 500 estimator fits. A candidate that fails is ranked last with its error.
candidates.title: Candidates

interval.description: Prediction interval computed for every candidate. Prediction interval as two quantiles [lower, upper] with 0 < lower < upper < 1, e.g. [0.1, 0.9] for 80 %. The baseline and ForecasterStats only take symmetric ones (lower + upper = 1). Null for the interval of the plan the strategy was built for.
interval.title: Interval

metric.description: Metric of every candidate. Metric, or list of metrics whose first one is the primary metric (the one that ranks); only the ones given are computed. Null for the metric chosen for the plan the strategy was built for, if one was chosen, else the one selected from the data.
metric.title: Metric

baseline.description: Whether to add a seasonal naive baseline (ForecasterEquivalentDate) to the ranking.
baseline.title: Baseline

ToolNotice.description:
A warning emitted while a tool call ran.

Attributes
----------
source : str
    Where the warning comes from: `'data'` (reading or profiling the
    data), `'plan'` (a warning the plan carries in `plan.warnings`, or
    the model a plan uses) or `'runtime'` (any other warning of the
    call).
category : str
    Class name of the warning (e.g. `'LongTrainingWarning'`), or
    `'ModelDownloadNotice'` for the notice of the server that a
    foundation model will download its weights.
message : str
    Text of the warning, without the suggestion of skforecast on how to
    silence it, cut to 1,000 characters.
count : int
    Number of times the call emitted it.
ToolNotice.title: ToolNotice

output_schema.description:
Envelope returned by the tools that create an object, and by
`describe_object`.

Attributes
----------
id : str
    Id of the object, to pass to the tools that take it.
kind : str
    Kind of the object: `'profile'`, `'plan'`, `'cv'`, `'backtest'`,
    `'comparison'` or `'forecast'`.
links : dict
    Ids of related objects: those it was built from (`profile_id`,
    `plan_id`, `cv_id`, and `parent_plan_id` for a refined plan), the
    plan of the winner of a comparison (`best_plan_id`), and the
    comparison a winning plan comes from (`comparison_id`).
summary : str
    Plain-text description of the object (`describe()` of the core),
    cut to 20,000 characters.
summary_truncated : bool
    Whether `summary` was cut; the full text is then in
    `files['summary']`.
notices : list of ToolNotice
    Warnings the call emitted, the first 20 distinct ones. Deprecation
    warnings go to the log of the server instead, and the failures of
    the candidates of a comparison are in its result.
notices_omitted : int
    Number of distinct warnings left out of `notices`.
files : dict
    Absolute paths of the files written for the object, by role:
    `predictions` and `metrics` (CSV with the index) of a backtest or a
    forecast, `leaderboard`, `best_predictions` and `best_metrics` of a
    comparison, and `summary` when the summary was cut.
values_included : bool
    Always False: the response holds no rows of the data or of the
    predictions. The summary carries statistics of the predictions, the
    metrics and the leaderboard of a comparison; the rows are in
    `files`.
cost : dict, None
    Cost of a cross-validation strategy, a backtest or a comparison:
    `n_folds`, `n_fits` (trainings of the forecaster in the shared
    strategy) and `estimator_fits` (fits of an estimator, which a
    direct forecaster multiplies by `steps`; for a comparison, the sum
    over its candidates). A cross-validation strategy also has
    `compare_estimator_fits`, the fits of a comparison without
    candidates with it. None for the other kinds.
changeable : list of str
    Arguments of `refine_plan` (for a plan) or of `create_cv` (for a
    cross-validation strategy) that build a variant of the object.
    Empty for the other kinds.
output_schema.title: ToolResult

name: forecast
description: Run a plan: forecast the future, or evaluate on a test set with `test_size`. Predictions and metrics go to CSV files. Returns a forecast id.

plan_id.description: Id of the plan to run (from `plan`, `refine_plan` or `links.best_plan_id` of `compare`).
plan_id.title: Plan Id

test_size.description: Null to forecast the future. To evaluate instead, the test set: the last n observations (an integer, which must equal `steps`) or the ISO 8601 date it starts at. A fraction in (0, 1) only works when it gives exactly `steps` observations.
test_size.title: Test Size

exog_path.description: Absolute path of a CSV file with the future values of the exogenous variables, one row per date (and series) of the horizon. Required to forecast the future when the plan uses exogenous variables. The script of `get_code` reads them from 'exog_future.csv' in its working directory.
exog_path.title: Exog Path

name: get_code
description: Return the Python script of an object: the one that ran, or that would run for a plan.

object_id.description: Id of a plan (its forecasting script), a cross-validation strategy (the code that builds it), a backtest, a forecast or a comparison (the script that ran).
object_id.title: Object Id

candidate.description: For a comparison, the candidate whose script to return. Null for the best one.
candidate.title: Candidate

output_schema.description:
Script of an object, returned by the `get_code` tool.

Attributes
----------
id : str
    Id of the object.
kind : str
    Kind of the object.
candidate : str, None
    Candidate of a comparison whose script it is.
code : str
    Python code, cut to 20,000 characters.
code_truncated : bool
    Whether `code` was cut; the full code is then in `files['code']`.
files : dict
    Absolute path of the file with the full code, when it was cut.
output_schema.title: CodeResult

name: get_failure
description: Return the traceback and the code of a failed run or of a failed candidate of a comparison.

object_id.description: `details.failure_id` of an error, or the id of a comparison whose candidate failed.
object_id.title: Object Id

candidate.description: Name of the failed candidate of a comparison.
candidate.title: Candidate

output_schema.description:
Full description of a failure, returned by the `get_failure` tool.

Attributes
----------
id : str
    Id of the failure, or of the comparison whose candidate failed.
candidate : str, None
    Candidate of the comparison that failed.
text : str
    Error, line and statement that failed, traceback and code that ran,
    cut to 20,000 characters. Like the messages of the errors, it can
    quote values of the data. The code that ran reads the data in memory,
    so it does not name the path of the data file.
text_truncated : bool
    Whether `text` was cut; the full text is then in `files['failure']`.
files : dict
    Absolute path of the file with the full text, when it was cut.
output_schema.title: FailureResult

name: list_objects
description: List the ids of the objects the server keeps.

kind.description: Only the objects of this kind. Null for every kind.
kind.title: Kind

ObjectInfo.description:
An object registered in the server, as listed by `list_objects`.

Attributes
----------
id : str
    Id of the object.
kind : str
    Kind of the object.
links : dict
    Ids of the objects it was built from.
ObjectInfo.title: ObjectInfo

output_schema.description:
Objects registered in the server, returned by `list_objects`.

Attributes
----------
objects : list of ObjectInfo
    Registered objects, most recently used first.
max_objects : int
    Most objects the server keeps; the least recently used ones are
    removed beyond it.
max_memory_mb : int
    Memory, in MB, the objects may take; the least recently used ones
    are removed beyond it.
removed : int
    Number of objects removed so far to stay within those limits. A
    tool that receives the id of a removed object says so.
output_schema.title: ObjectList

name: describe_object
description: Return the response that created an object (summary, links, notices, files).
